subject: Dedicated fit assessment — recap, isolation ask, and procurement path
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Park <zoe@quantum.ai>, Arun Mitra <arun@quantum.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T15:02:00Z
Subject: Dedicated fit assessment — recap, isolation ask, and procurement path

Hi Zoe / Arun —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Please reply if I missed anything.

Top pain points you mentioned
- Inference variability: spikes during model retraining/experiments are causing missed p99 latency targets in production (current p99 ~1.4s, target <= 400ms).
- Data isolation: models must never share KV/prefix caches with other tenants; strict tenancy boundary required for PHI/PII workloads.
- Cost predictability: finance needs a monthly predictable line item rather than bursty cloud spend.

Primary goals
- Reserve capacity for a mid-size production fleet (initial commit target: 8–12 A100-equivalent GPUs) with clear isolation and burst capacity.
- Maintain <400ms p99 for 2k QPS mixed-gen traffic with caching & batching.
- SOC 2 evidence and audit logs for inference requests by customer token.

What we propose (high level)
- Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) with tenant-isolated pools (VM/GPU level isolation + software tenancy knobs), optional single-tenant nodes for PHI paths.
- Autoscale policy with burst buckets: base reserved + 20% burst on-demand for short spikes.
- Initial SLA target: 99.95% uptime with 10% latency headroom and automatic fallback to smaller-cost model variant on pressure.

Information we need from your side to size & price
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS (per region).
2) Typical request sequence length and model families (decoder-only, encoder-decoder).
3) Percentage of requests that require PHI isolation vs general traffic.
4) Any compliance delivery requirements (SOC 2 evidence window, logging retention timeframe).

Procurement and timeline
- Ballpark pricing: we will send a committed-capacity quote once we have sizing inputs above; expect a 30–45 day procurement/PO cadence for a new reserved pool contract.
- If procurement needs a template SOW/PO language, I can share our standard.

Next steps (proposed)
- Zoe: send QPS + percent-phi split by Wed 10/21.
- We: share a one-page MOP (attached) and a preliminary sizing/ops-runbook by Thu 10/22.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (ops + networking) — propose Fri 10/23 11:00 AM PT.

Attachments: quantumai-mop-v1.pdf (summary of operational responsibilities), qai-network-diagram.png

Thanks —
Marcus

Subject: Re: Dedicated fit assessment — recap, isolation ask, and procurement path

Thanks Marcus — appreciated. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic profile: steady-state 1.1k QPS (US-east), peak 3.6k QPS (short bursts ~5–7 minutes) during nightly model refresh windows.
2) Sequence lengths: median 64 tokens, 95th percentile 320 tokens. Primary family: decoder-only LLMs.
3) PHI split: roughly 12% of requests need PHI isolation and stricter logging.
4) Compliance: we are SOC 2 Type II in process; we need evidence of request-level audit logs for a 90-day retention period.

On procurement — our finance team typically needs: line-item quote, MSA redlines, and a PO template. We will loop procurement on the deep-dive.

Also: can you confirm whether the "burst bucket" model will incur separate overage charges or is blended into the reserved plan pricing? If overage, please give a rough delta.

Zoe

Looping in preliminary ops sizing comments — high level numbers only. Marcus, flag anything you want tightened before we send to the customer.

Prelim sizing (assumptions based on Zoe's QPS/seq profile):
- Baseline reserve: 10x A100-eq GPUs (mixed precision q4_0 / q8x optimizations) to hit steady-state 1.1k QPS with median sequences.
- Burst headroom: additional 3x on-demand GPUs for 5–10 minute windows (auto-attach).
- PHI isolation: recommend 2 dedicated single-tenant nodes (A100-eq) for PHI traffic path — avoids multi-tenant cache sharing and simplifies audit delineation.
- Network: private peering (VPC) with 10 Gbps link; need your network CIDR and firewall egress rules.

SLA and reg: 99.95% uptime baseline, proposal includes 30 second cold-start mitigations and secondary fallback model variant on degraded capacity. We'll draft clear SLO/SLA language for the next doc.

I'll drop a short sizing slide into the shared Drive and attach a one-page MOP we can ship to procurement.

— Priyom
